title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 117
paragraphs: So Harpagos declared the truth, and Astyages, concealing the anger he held against him for what had come to pass, first related the matter over again to Harpagos just as he had been told it by the herdsman. Then, when it had been thus repeated, he ended by saying that the child was alive and that what had come to pass was well. “For,” he continued, “I was greatly troubled by what had been done to this child, and I thought it no light thing that I had been at variance with my daughter. Therefore, consider this a happy change of fortune. First send your son to be with the boy who is newly come, and then, since I intend to make a sacrifice of thanksgiving for the preservation of the boy to those gods to whom that honor belongs, be here yourself to dine with me.”
